learningObjective: Add, grow, convert, snapshot and remove managed disks. Choose and set up the right encryption, especially encryption at host.
engineer: Disk operations: attach or detach data disks while the VM runs; make a disk bigger, never smaller (data disks can often grow without downtime, then you extend the partition in the OS); change the disk type, for example Standard SSD to Premium SSD, with the VM deallocated; take incremental snapshots, for backup or copying; set host caching per disk (None, ReadOnly or ReadWrite).
Disk limits: the VM size decides the maximum number of data disks and the total speed (IOPS and throughput).
Disk speed: Premium SSD gets faster as it gets bigger (P-tiers). With Premium SSD v2 and Ultra, you set speed separately from size. They have limits: Ultra can't be an OS disk, and both need zones.

Encryption options: server-side encryption (SSE) with platform-managed keys, the default and always on; SSE with your own keys, through a disk encryption set that points to a Key Vault key; encryption at host, where data is encrypted on the VM's host and stays encrypted all the way to storage; Azure Disk Encryption (ADE), the old option, which encrypts inside the VM.

What encryption at host adds: the temporary disk and ephemeral OS disk are encrypted with platform keys. The caches of the OS and data disks use the same key type as each disk (add a disk encryption set for your own keys).
Step 1, register once per subscription: az feature register --namespace Microsoft.Compute --name EncryptionAtHost, then wait until it shows Registered.
Step 2, pick a supported size: older sizes don't support it. The size (SKU) must have the capability EncryptionAtHostSupported.

Step 3, turn it on: new VM, on the portal's Disks tab, tick Encryption at host; existing VM, deallocate it, go to VM > Disks > Additional settings, turn on Encryption at host, save and start; scale sets, only VMs created after you turn it on are encrypted.
Azure Disk Encryption (ADE): uses BitLocker (Windows) or DM-Crypt (Linux) inside the VM. Keys go in a Key Vault in the same region and subscription.

ADE is retiring on 15 September 2028: after that date, ADE disks won't unlock when the VM restarts. You can't turn on encryption at host on a VM that has, or ever had, ADE. Moving off ADE means new disks on a new VM.
Confidential disk encryption: available for confidential VMs.

example.title: Growing a full data disk
body: A database VM's 128 GiB data disk is 95% full. The admin grows it to 256 GiB in the portal while the VM runs, then extends the volume in Disk Management.

Then security asks for the temporary disk and caches to be encrypted too. The admin registers EncryptionAtHost, deallocates the VM, turns on Encryption at host under Disks > Additional settings, and starts the VM again.

architectureDecisions: Production databases: use Premium SSD (or Premium SSD v2).
New VMs: use encryption at host, and add a disk encryption set if you need your own keys. Move off ADE before 15 September 2028.
Take a snapshot first: before any risky change.

misconceptions.myth: Disks aren't encrypted unless you turn on extra encryption.
misconceptions.reality: No. SSE with platform keys is always on. Encryption at host adds the temporary disk and caches.

misconceptions.myth: You can switch an ADE VM to encryption at host in place.
misconceptions.reality: No. It's blocked on any VM that ever had ADE. Create a new VM with new disks.

misconceptions.myth: You can change a disk to Premium while the VM runs.
misconceptions.reality: No. Changing disk type needs the VM deallocated.

misconceptions.myth: Data on the temporary disk survives a redeploy.
misconceptions.reality: No. The temporary disk is wiped.

comparisons.difference: Block volumes, like managed disks. gp3 and io2, where you set speed separately, are like Premium SSD v2 and Ultra.
Shared file storage over SMB or NFS, not a disk attached to one VM.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't make a disk smaller.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a smaller disk and copy the data.

troubleshooting.symptom: Encryption at host is greyed out or fails.
troubleshooting.cause: The feature isn't registered, the VM size isn't supported, the VM is still running, or the VM had Azure Disk Encryption.
troubleshooting.fix: Register EncryptionAtHost, resize to a supported size, and deallocate. For VMs that had ADE, move to a new VM.

troubleshooting.symptom: The new disk size doesn't show in the OS.
troubleshooting.fix: Extend the volume (Disk Management on Windows; growpart and resize2fs on Linux).

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't attach another data disk.
troubleshooting.cause: The VM size's disk limit is reached.
troubleshooting.fix: Resize the VM to one with more data disk slots.

configuration.limits: Changing disk type needs the VM deallocated
The VM size sets the maximum number of data disks
Turning on encryption at host for an existing VM needs it deallocated
Encryption at host is blocked on VMs that ever had ADE
configuration.permissions: Virtual Machine Contributor, for disk and VM operations
Key Vault key access for the disk encryption set's managed identity (for your own keys)
configuration.prerequisites: A VM size that supports the disk type
For encryption at host: the EncryptionAtHost feature registered, a supported VM size, and no Azure Disk Encryption on the VM, now or before
